1	# Vortex Continuous Integration — Catalog-Driven, Driver-Sliceable Test Architecture
2	
3	Vortex tests are **declarative data** run by **pytest**, replacing the imperative,
4	driver-pinned bash that used to live in `ci/regression.sh`. `blackbox.sh` stays the
5	unchanged executor. `ci/regression.sh` is now slim and serves two roles: the **local
6	entry point** into the catalog (`--all` / `--test <selector>`, thin wrappers over
7	`pytest [-m …] ci`) and the **host/multi-step backend** for the four categories that
8	don't fit the common shape (`dtm`, `sst`, `gem5`, `cupbop`), which the catalog's
9	`via: script` cases reach through the internal `--run <flow>`. This document covers both
10	halves: the **engine** (test cases + pytest harness) and the **workflow** (GitHub fan-out
11	+ planner).
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. Problem
16	
17	`ci/regression.sh.in` *was* the core CI engine: ~1400 lines of imperative bash, ~30
18	category functions, **401 driver-pinned invocations** in three execution styles —
19	326 `./ci/blackbox.sh --driver=<d> …`, 75 `make -C … run-<d>`, and 16 standalone
20	`make -C sim/<d>` builds. The driver (`simx`/`rtlsim`/`xrtsim`/`opaesim`) is hard-coded
21	into every line. That single fact is the root of every limitation:
22	
23	| # | Pathology | Consequence |
24	|---|-----------|-------------|
25	| P1 | Driver baked into every line | Can't run "simx only" without editing 401 lines — yet `rtlsim` (~168 runs, the Verilator long pole) dominates cost. |
26	| P2 | Three execution styles, no single seam | No one place to filter, time, or report a test. |
27	| P3 | Tests are code, not data | Coverage is unqueryable; path-selection must be a hand-kept regex; no per-test report. |
28	| P4 | Build/run entangled | A `(driver, CONFIGS)` sim is re-elaborated whenever the config changes between adjacent lines (388 cases span 239 distinct sim builds; e.g. riscv's 11 cases rebuild a sim that 2 builds would cover). |
29	| P5 | `CONFIGS` as repeated env prefixes | The documented footgun: app and driver must be built with matching `CONFIGS` or results are silently wrong. |
30	| P6 | Category = coarse unit | One function = one CI job = all its drivers + configs, serially. |
31	| P7 | No metadata | No `tier`, `needs`, `touches`, `xlen`-applicability per test. |
32	| P8 | `set -e` fragility | Inline driver-gating must dance around errexit. |
33	
34	Every attempt to *retrofit* a driver filter onto this (a blackbox gate, a `run_test`
35	wrapper, `make run-` guards, `set -e` workarounds) fights P1–P3. Making tests **data**
36	dissolves the problem: the slice becomes a query.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. Model: a test case is a point in an N-dimensional space
41	
42	Axes that today are flattened into one bash line, kept explicit so any one can become a
43	*filter* or a *matrix dimension*:
44	
45	```
46	category   amo, cache, tensor, graphics, …
47	driver     simx | rtlsim | xrtsim | opaesim          (cost axis)
48	xlen       32 | 64                                    (build-tree axis)
49	config     CONFIGS="-DVX_CFG_…"                        (rebuild axis)
50	shape      cores/warps/threads/l2/l3, args
51	tier       smoke | full | nightly                     (when-to-run axis)
52	needs      (none) | mpi | sst | gem5                  (env axis)
53	touches    source paths this case exercises           (selection axis)
54	```
55	
56	---
57	
58	## 3. Engine
59	
60	Three things we own — **test-case data + thin pytest glue + the unchanged executor**;
61	everything else (selection, parallelism, reporting) is pytest.
62	
63	```
64	   ci/testcases/*.yaml        markers/-m, -k, --changed     ┌──────────────┐
65	   (data: cases)  ───────────────────────────────────────▶ │    pytest    │
66	                     testcase.py + conftest.py + test_runner.py  (the runner)│
67	                                                            └──────┬───────┘
68	                                              fixture: build│once per build-key
69	                                                       ┌────▼────────┐  run many
70	                                                       │  executor   │  per case
71	                                                       │ blackbox.sh │  (UNCHANGED)
72	                                                       └────┬────────┘
73	                                            --junitxml ┌────▼────────┐
74	                                                       │  reporter   │ → GitHub test report
75	                                                       └─────────────┘
76	```
77	
78	### 3.1 Test cases (`ci/testcases/<category>.yaml`)
79	
80	One file per category; fields map 1:1 to existing `blackbox.sh` flags, so it is a
81	faithful transcription, not a reinterpretation. An entry with `drivers: [...]` expands
82	to one case per driver. `xlen` is an **outer** dimension — a collection-time filter
83	against the ambient build tree, never expanded here (build32/ and build64/ are separate
84	trees).
85	
86	```yaml
87	category: amo
88	defaults:
89	  configs: "-DVX_CFG_EXT_A_ENABLE"
90	  xlen: [32, 64]
91	  tier: smoke
92	  touches: [hw/rtl/cache, sim/simx/amo, sim/simx/mem]
93	tests:
94	  - id: base
95	    app: amo
96	    drivers: [simx, rtlsim]                 # -> 2 cases
97	
98	  - id: wb-dirtybytes1
99	    app: amo
100	    drivers: [rtlsim]
101	    configs+: "-DVX_CFG_DCACHE_WRITEBACK=1 -DVX_CFG_DCACHE_DIRTYBYTES=1 -DVX_CFG_DCACHE_NUM_WAYS=4"
102	
103	  - id: mc-l3
104	    app: amo
105	    drivers: [simx]
106	    configs+: "-DVX_CFG_L2_WRITEBACK=0"
107	    shape: {cores: 4, l2cache: true, l3cache: true}
108	    args: "-n8"
109	    tier: full
110	```
111	
112	The three execution styles collapse into one `via` field:
113	
114	```yaml
115	  # make-run (riscv ISA, vulkan, hip, rvc, vm). {driver}/{xlen} are substituted.
116	  - {id: isa, via: make-run, dir: tests/riscv/isa, target: "run-{driver}-{xlen}a", drivers: [simx, rtlsim]}
117	
118	  # script — the host/python categories (unittest, synthesis, vector, dtm, sst, gem5,
119	  # cupbop). Driverless cases self-build. `needs:` records the env a cell must
120	  # provision (it drives the workflow profile); it does NOT skip — a missing dep fails.
121	  - {id: legacy, via: script, run: "./ci/regression.sh --sst", needs: [sst]}
122	```
123	
124	`configs` overrides the default; `configs+` appends. Metadata absent today —
125	`tier`/`needs`/`touches`/`xlen` — is first-class.
126	
127	### 3.2 The runner is pytest, not a hand-rolled engine
128	
129	A test runner — load, select, run, report — is a solved problem, so we **adopt the
130	industry standard** (`ctest` is ruled out: it is CMake's, and Vortex is GNU-Make-only).
131	pytest supplies the machinery; we write three small files of glue and **no config
132	file** — pytest's own conventions (a `conftest.py`, `test_`-prefixed test module,
133	markers) carry it.
134	
135	| Need | pytest mechanism |
136	|------|------------------|
137	| case → test matrix | `pytest_generate_tests` parametrizes from the data |
138	| selection (driver/tier/category) | one **marker per value** + `-m "cache and simx and smoke"` |
139	| build-once-run-many | a fixture scoped to the `(driver, CONFIGS)` build-key |
140	| report | `--junitxml` (the universal CI interchange format) |
141	| parallelism | across GitHub matrix cells (serial within a cell — see §6) |
142	| dry-run "what would run" | `--collect-only` |
143	
144	**Three files, all in `ci/`** — the conventional pytest layout (support module +
145	`conftest.py` + test module):
146	- `ci/testcase.py` — the `Spec` model + loaders + the planner **CLI** (`lint`/`matrix`/
147	  `select`). No pytest dependency, so the lightweight plan job imports it freely.
148	- `ci/conftest.py` — the hooks/fixtures: `pytest_configure` registers **markers derived
149	  from the data** (so adding a category/driver needs no edit, and `--strict-markers`
150	  catches `-m` typos), `pytest_generate_tests` parametrizes + applies one marker per
151	  value + the ambient-XLEN filter, and the `sim_build` fixture builds each
152	  `(driver,CONFIGS)` once (the P4 fix). Cases run **serially within a cell** — the
153	  parallelism is across GitHub matrix cells, each its own build tree — so successive
154	  `CONFIGS` never clobber a `sim/` build that is still in use (see §6).
155	- `ci/test_runner.py` — the single `test_case` that shells out to `blackbox.sh`/`make`
156	  and asserts a clean exit. Every failure (and every build warning escalated to an
157	  error) is a real, red failure — except a case carrying a `known_issue:` reason in
158	  the catalog, which `conftest.py` turns into a tracked `xfail`: it still builds and
159	  runs, but its failure is expected and does not fail CI (an unexpected pass surfaces
160	  as `XPASS`). Reserve it for triaged, documented breakage.
161	
162	No `pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini`: markers register dynamically in `conftest.py`,
163	`test_runner.py` is auto-discovered by the `test_` prefix, and the run passes `ci` as the
164	path. `blackbox.sh` is untouched; `regression.sh` is reduced to the four host/multi-step
165	backends (§5).
166	
167	Selection is idiomatic pytest:
168	
169	```
170	VX_XLEN=32 pytest ci -m "cache and simx and smoke" --strict-markers
171	pytest ci --collect-only -q -m "simx"      # dry-run
172	```
173	
174	### 3.3 Cross-driver checks (`check: model_parity`)
175	
176	SimX is the timing model of the RTL, not just a functional oracle. A case with
177	`check: model_parity` validates that: it is **not** driver-expanded — the runner
178	executes the same app/args/configs on **simx and rtlsim** as two legs of one case
179	(pinned to the rtlsim driver for build/matrix placement, since it elaborates the
180	RTL) and compares the runtime's final `PERF: instrs=…, cycles=…` summary:
181	
182	- **instrs must match exactly** — both drivers are deterministic ISA-level
183	  executions, so any delta is functional divergence, not a timing gap;
184	- **cycles must agree within `tolerance`** (default 5%, per-case override).
185	
186	Every case also prints a `PARITY:` line with both counts and the measured gap, so
187	green runs still leave a trend trail in the logs. The general-pipeline matrix
188	(vecadd, sgemm) lives in `ci/testcases/model_parity.yaml`; each extension
189	(tensor*, raytracing, graphics TEX/RASTER/OM, dxa) carries its own
190	`model_parity-*` case in its category file, with only that extension enabled so a
191	regression is attributable. Workloads are sized so steady state dominates
192	(>=~300k cycles for the pipeline cases) — a tiny kernel is all boot/dispatch skew
193	and makes the gap ratio noisy. A `model_parity` marker selects them all:
194	`pytest ci -m model_parity`. Use `known_issue:` (not a loosened tolerance) for a
195	tracked gap under investigation.
196	
197	The `model_parity` category (`ci/testcases/model_parity.yaml`) is a **dedicated
198	cell**: because every `check: model_parity` case also carries the `model_parity`
199	marker, the `model_parity` cell runs `-m "model_parity and rtlsim"` and thereby
200	sweeps *every* parity case catalog-wide — one centralized simx↔RTL gate across
201	`{xlen 32, xlen 64}`. It runs at **`full`** tier (rtlsim-heavy → PR + nightly).
202	So a parity case never double-runs: category cells exclude the check markers
203	(`… and not model_parity and not perf_gate`); the check cells own them.
204	
205	### 3.4 Perf-regression checks (`check: perf_gate`)
206	
207	Same gating shape as §3.3 (its own dedicated cell driven by the `perf_gate`
208	marker, `full` tier, rtlsim-pinned) but a different assertion: instead of
209	comparing SimX vs RTL, it compares **this commit's rtlsim cycles against a
210	checked-in golden baseline** within ±2% (`ci/perf_baseline.py`). Because rtlsim
211	cycle counts are deterministic and host-independent, there is no noise to handle —
212	the threshold only absorbs benign, intended micro-changes.
213	
214	- **Baselines** live in the source tree at `ci/perf/baselines/<category>.json`
215	  (canonical sorted JSON, one file per category). Each entry stores the measured
216	  `cycles`/`instrs` per xlen, plus a `config_hash` (of app/args/configs/shape)
217	  and the workload's `instrs` as **staleness guards**: if the run config changes
218	  (`config_hash` mismatch) or the workload changes (`instrs` mismatch), the check
219	  errors "regenerate" instead of comparing stale numbers.
220	- **Direction**: cycles above baseline by >tolerance = **regression** (hard fail);
221	  cycles below by >tolerance = an unlocked **improvement** — also fails, asking
222	  you to update the baseline so the gain is ratcheted in and a later silent
223	  regression back toward the old number is still caught.
224	- **Updating** is script-generated + human-reviewed, never done by CI:
225	  `pytest ci -m perf_gate --update-baselines` (a `conftest.py` option that
226	  flips `_perf_gate` from assert- to record-mode and flushes on session
227	  finish). A human runs it only for an intended perf change, reviews the JSON
228	  diff (`cycles: 999027 → 918400` = an explicit, reviewable perf delta), and
229	  commits. **CI must never pass `--update-baselines`** — an auto-updated baseline
230	  would silently absorb every regression. Same discipline as a golden image.
231	- Benchmarks **reuse the steady-state model_parity workloads** (base pipeline in
232	  `ci/testcases/perf_gate.yaml`; extensions as `perf_gate-*` cases in
233	  their category files) — one run, its own gate.
234	
235	---
236	
237	## 4. Workflow
238	
239	### 4.1 `ci.yml` — catalog-driven
240	
241	`plan` reads the data (via `testcase.py matrix`, no build env) and emits the
242	`(category × driver × xlen)` cell list for this event; each cell runs
243	`pytest ci -m "<category> and <driver>"` in its build tree, emits JUnit, and the run is
244	gated by a single `complete` job.
245	
246	```
247	plan:  event × driver-policy × tier × (touches[] ∩ diff)  ->  cells JSON
248	setup: warm toolchain + third_party caches once (setup-vortex prepare=true)
249	build: one build tree per xlen, needs setup (restores the warmed caches)
250	tests: matrix = cells  ->  pytest ci -m "<cat> and <driver>" per cell  ->  JUnit
251	complete: single green gate (needs plan+setup+build+tests)
252	```
253	
254	`setup` exists so a cold cache prepares the toolchain (a prebuilt-tarball download)
255	and third_party **once**, not once per xlen: the two `build` jobs `needs: setup` and
256	only restore. On a cache hit it is a fast no-op.
257	
258	Driver/tier policy by event:
259	
260	| Trigger | Drivers | Tier |
261	|---------|---------|------|
262	| push | simx | smoke |
263	| pull_request | simx, rtlsim | smoke,full |
264	| schedule (nightly/weekly) | all | all |
265	| workflow_dispatch | (inputs) | (inputs) |
266	
267	This is the whole point: a push runs `simx` (the cheap, high-signal driver) and defers
268	the ~168 `rtlsim` runs to PR-gate/nightly — `--drivers=simx` is now just `-m "simx"`.
269	
270	### 4.2 `setup-vortex` composite action
271	
272	The cache/deps boilerplate (`read-version-pins + cache toolchain + cache third-party +
273	install deps + pip`) is one local composite action, parameterized by `profile`
274	(lite/full), used by every job. A `prepare` input (true only in the `setup` job) makes
275	it additionally **populate** the caches on a miss — building the toolchain + third_party
276	once — so build/test jobs (`prepare: false`) only ever restore. Prep logic lives in the
277	action, not duplicated across jobs.
278	
279	### 4.3 `apptainer-ci.yml` — share setup, not orchestration
280	
281	The Apptainer flow validates the build/test works **inside the `vortex.sif` container** —
282	an *environmental* signal, not functional coverage the host run already provides.
283	It is deliberately **not** folded into `ci.yml` (different intent → the wrong
284	abstraction). It stays a separate, minimal workflow that:
285	- **reuses** the `setup-vortex` composite action (genuinely identical host-side work), and
286	- runs a representative `pytest ci -m "regression and simx"` slice inside the container, not the
287	  full matrix.
288	
289	Recommended triggers: weekly **offset** from the host weekly (so a failure is attributable
290	to the container, not the code) plus `paths:` on the container-definition files.
291	
292	---
293	
294	## 5. Migration — done
295	
296	The catalog is now the **single source of truth**; `ci/regression.sh.in` no longer
297	duplicates any cataloged test. Final shape:
298	
299	- **25 categories native** in the catalog (`via: blackbox`/`make-run`/`script`), including
300	  the host categories `unittest`, `synthesis`, `vector` (self-contained `via: script` that
301	  call `make` directly — no `regression.sh`).
302	- **MX coverage is first-class:** `tensor_mx` (transcribed from the legacy `tensor_mx()`,
303	  incl. a `-DTCU_MX_TLS` tensor-level-scale variant) and `tensor_sp_mx` are catalog
304	  categories. `TCU_MX_TLS` is a **sw/test macro** passed per-case in `configs`, **not** a
305	  hardware `VX_CFG_` knob (it is not in `VX_config.toml`).
306	- **4 host/multi-step categories** (`dtm`, `sst`, `gem5`, `cupbop`) stay `via: script`
307	  delegating to `./ci/regression.sh --<cat>`. These are genuinely multi-step host flows
308	  (special builds: `USE_SST=1`/`USE_GEM5=1`, the gem5 ARM matrix, a cupbop download) that
309	  don't fit the common shape, so `regression.sh.in` is **kept on purpose** — slimmed from
310	  ~1400 lines to ~320, holding only those four functions. This is the documented
311	  steady state, not a pending deletion.
312	- **440 test cases / 31 categories**; `ci/testcase.py lint` + `pytest --collect-only` clean.
313	- Local runs go through `ci/regression.sh` against the **same** catalog CI runs, so
314	  they can never drift from it: `./ci/regression.sh --all` runs every category for the
315	  build tree's XLEN, and `./ci/regression.sh --test "<selector>"` runs a slice, where
316	  `<selector>` is a pytest marker expression — a category (`tensor`), a driver
317	  (`rtlsim`), or a combo (`"tensor and simx"`). Both wrap `pytest [-m …] ci`.
318	
319	Real per-category sim execution runs on CI, not locally.
320	
321	### 5.1 Graphics / Vulkan fixed-function coverage
322	
323	The graphics stack is swept along the **fixed-function (FF) axis** — each of TEX /
324	RASTER / OM either present in hardware or emulated in SIMT software — because the
325	FF↔SIMT boundary is the recurring graphics bug surface:
326	
327	- **Native FF units** (`graphics`): `gfx_tex` / `gfx_raster` / `gfx_om` each drive
328	  one FF unit; `gfx_draw3d` drives all three (TEX+RASTER+OM).
329	- **Early-Z** (`graphics`, `gfx_earlyz-*`): `gfx_draw3d` built with
330	  `-DVX_CFG_RASTER_EARLYZ` — the opt-in occlusion-cull knob (legal only with
331	  OM+RASTER; off by default → raster byte-identical). Bit-identical to the
332	  no-early-Z golden on box@128 / evilskull@32 (simx + rtlsim); evilskull@128
333	  carries a tracked 2-px in-flight-write residual (`known_issue`).
334	- **FF/SW mix + full software emulation** (`vulkan`, `ff-*`): the vortexpipe 3D
335	  pipeline (`draw3d`) with per-unit drop knobs — `NO_TEX` / `NO_RASTER` / `NO_OM`
336	  (`tests/vulkan/common.mk`) — sweeps every FF/SW combination
337	  (`ff-raster-tex-om` … `ff-om-only`, and `ff-all-sw` = whole pipeline in SIMT
338	  software). vortexpipe routes each dropped unit to the `gfx_*_sw` ABI, validated
339	  against the same golden as the all-hardware path. Combos that need SW-TEX or
340	  SW-RASTER routing are `known_issue` until vortexpipe wires those stages (the SW
341	  ABI already exists).
342	- **Ray tracing + hybrid** (`vulkan`): `rt-raytrace` / `rt-rtquery` (VK_KHR_ray_query
343	  benchmarks on the PRISM RTU), `gfx-rt-rtquery-id` (rasterized fragment shader +
344	  inline ray query — gfx + RT in one frame), and `gfx-multidraw` (multi-drawcall
345	  rasterization). The blanket `vulkan` `isa-*` cases still run the whole suite per
346	  driver; these track the individual scenarios and add the FF/SW-mix builds the
347	  suite does not produce.
348	
349	New cases in these yaml files are auto-included in the plan (§4.1) — no workflow
350	edit needed. `known_issue` cases still build and run (surfacing an `XPASS` when the
351	underlying support lands), so aspirational coverage is tracked, not silently absent.
352	
353	---
354	
355	## 6. Risks & mitigations
356	
357	- **Build-dedup vs. parallelism (resolved).** Successive `CONFIGS` build into the same
358	  `sim/` output, so building different keys concurrently in one tree clobbers them — this
359	  was confirmed on the first CI run (an in-tree `pytest -n auto` raced multiple Verilator
360	  builds and most cells errored). Resolution: **cases run serially within a cell**, and
361	  parallelism is taken **across GitHub matrix cells** (each cell is its own runner +
362	  build tree). A future intra-cell speedup would need per-worker isolated trees
363	  (`git worktree`); not worth it now.
364	- **Data drifts from reality.** `testcase.py lint` runs in CI; each migrated category is
365	  parity-diffed against its legacy function once before the bash is deleted.
366	- **Script categories.** `via: script` lets the special categories delegate to legacy
367	  without forcing them into the common shape; their `needs` deps must be provisioned by
368	  the workflow (a missing dep is a real failure — nothing is skipped).
369	- **pytest dependency.** Industry standard; Python is already on the CI path; pinned like
370	  any dev tool. The harness only orchestrates and shells out.
371	- **Catalog format: YAML** — list-of-records ergonomics, PyYAML/Actions-native; TOML is
372	  awkward for record arrays, JSON loses comments.
373

# Vortex Continuous Integration — Catalog-Driven, Driver-Sliceable Test Architecture

Vortex tests are **declarative data** run by **pytest**, replacing the imperative,
driver-pinned bash that used to live in `ci/regression.sh`. `blackbox.sh` stays the
unchanged executor. `ci/regression.sh` is now slim and serves two roles: the **local
entry point** into the catalog (`--all` / `--test <selector>`, thin wrappers over
`pytest [-m …] ci`) and the **host/multi-step backend** for the four categories that
don't fit the common shape (`dtm`, `sst`, `gem5`, `cupbop`), which the catalog's
`via: script` cases reach through the internal `--run <flow>`. This document covers both
halves: the **engine** (test cases + pytest harness) and the **workflow** (GitHub fan-out
+ planner).

---

## 1. Problem

`ci/regression.sh.in` *was* the core CI engine: ~1400 lines of imperative bash, ~30
category functions, **401 driver-pinned invocations** in three execution styles —
326 `./ci/blackbox.sh --driver=<d> …`, 75 `make -C … run-<d>`, and 16 standalone
`make -C sim/<d>` builds. The driver (`simx`/`rtlsim`/`xrtsim`/`opaesim`) is hard-coded
into every line. That single fact is the root of every limitation:

| # | Pathology | Consequence |
|---|-----------|-------------|
| P1 | Driver baked into every line | Can't run "simx only" without editing 401 lines — yet `rtlsim` (~168 runs, the Verilator long pole) dominates cost. |
| P2 | Three execution styles, no single seam | No one place to filter, time, or report a test. |
| P3 | Tests are code, not data | Coverage is unqueryable; path-selection must be a hand-kept regex; no per-test report. |
| P4 | Build/run entangled | A `(driver, CONFIGS)` sim is re-elaborated whenever the config changes between adjacent lines (388 cases span 239 distinct sim builds; e.g. riscv's 11 cases rebuild a sim that 2 builds would cover). |
| P5 | `CONFIGS` as repeated env prefixes | The documented footgun: app and driver must be built with matching `CONFIGS` or results are silently wrong. |
| P6 | Category = coarse unit | One function = one CI job = all its drivers + configs, serially. |
| P7 | No metadata | No `tier`, `needs`, `touches`, `xlen`-applicability per test. |
| P8 | `set -e` fragility | Inline driver-gating must dance around errexit. |

Every attempt to *retrofit* a driver filter onto this (a blackbox gate, a `run_test`
wrapper, `make run-` guards, `set -e` workarounds) fights P1–P3. Making tests **data**
dissolves the problem: the slice becomes a query.

---

## 2. Model: a test case is a point in an N-dimensional space

Axes that today are flattened into one bash line, kept explicit so any one can become a
*filter* or a *matrix dimension*:

```
category   amo, cache, tensor, graphics, …
driver     simx | rtlsim | xrtsim | opaesim          (cost axis)
xlen       32 | 64                                    (build-tree axis)
config     CONFIGS="-DVX_CFG_…"                        (rebuild axis)
shape      cores/warps/threads/l2/l3, args
tier       smoke | full | nightly                     (when-to-run axis)
needs      (none) | mpi | sst | gem5                  (env axis)
touches    source paths this case exercises           (selection axis)
```

---

## 3. Engine

Three things we own — **test-case data + thin pytest glue + the unchanged executor**;
everything else (selection, parallelism, reporting) is pytest.

```
   ci/testcases/*.yaml        markers/-m, -k, --changed     ┌──────────────┐
   (data: cases)  ───────────────────────────────────────▶ │    pytest    │
                     testcase.py + conftest.py + test_runner.py  (the runner)│
                                                            └──────┬───────┘
                                              fixture: build│once per build-key
                                                       ┌────▼────────┐  run many
                                                       │  executor   │  per case
                                                       │ blackbox.sh │  (UNCHANGED)
                                                       └────┬────────┘
                                            --junitxml ┌────▼────────┐
                                                       │  reporter   │ → GitHub test report
                                                       └─────────────┘
```

### 3.1 Test cases (`ci/testcases/<category>.yaml`)

One file per category; fields map 1:1 to existing `blackbox.sh` flags, so it is a
faithful transcription, not a reinterpretation. An entry with `drivers: [...]` expands
to one case per driver. `xlen` is an **outer** dimension — a collection-time filter
against the ambient build tree, never expanded here (build32/ and build64/ are separate
trees).

```yaml
category: amo
defaults:
  configs: "-DVX_CFG_EXT_A_ENABLE"
  xlen: [32, 64]
  tier: smoke
  touches: [hw/rtl/cache, sim/simx/amo, sim/simx/mem]
tests:
  - id: base
    app: amo
    drivers: [simx, rtlsim]                 # -> 2 cases

  - id: wb-dirtybytes1
    app: amo
    drivers: [rtlsim]
    configs+: "-DVX_CFG_DCACHE_WRITEBACK=1 -DVX_CFG_DCACHE_DIRTYBYTES=1 -DVX_CFG_DCACHE_NUM_WAYS=4"

  - id: mc-l3
    app: amo
    drivers: [simx]
    configs+: "-DVX_CFG_L2_WRITEBACK=0"
    shape: {cores: 4, l2cache: true, l3cache: true}
    args: "-n8"
    tier: full
```

The three execution styles collapse into one `via` field:

```yaml
  # make-run (riscv ISA, vulkan, hip, rvc, vm). {driver}/{xlen} are substituted.
  - {id: isa, via: make-run, dir: tests/riscv/isa, target: "run-{driver}-{xlen}a", drivers: [simx, rtlsim]}

  # script — the host/python categories (unittest, synthesis, vector, dtm, sst, gem5,
  # cupbop). Driverless cases self-build. `needs:` records the env a cell must
  # provision (it drives the workflow profile); it does NOT skip — a missing dep fails.
  - {id: legacy, via: script, run: "./ci/regression.sh --sst", needs: [sst]}
```

`configs` overrides the default; `configs+` appends. Metadata absent today —
`tier`/`needs`/`touches`/`xlen` — is first-class.

### 3.2 The runner is pytest, not a hand-rolled engine

A test runner — load, select, run, report — is a solved problem, so we **adopt the
industry standard** (`ctest` is ruled out: it is CMake's, and Vortex is GNU-Make-only).
pytest supplies the machinery; we write three small files of glue and **no config
file** — pytest's own conventions (a `conftest.py`, `test_`-prefixed test module,
markers) carry it.

| Need | pytest mechanism |
|------|------------------|
| case → test matrix | `pytest_generate_tests` parametrizes from the data |
| selection (driver/tier/category) | one **marker per value** + `-m "cache and simx and smoke"` |
| build-once-run-many | a fixture scoped to the `(driver, CONFIGS)` build-key |
| report | `--junitxml` (the universal CI interchange format) |
| parallelism | across GitHub matrix cells (serial within a cell — see §6) |
| dry-run "what would run" | `--collect-only` |

**Three files, all in `ci/`** — the conventional pytest layout (support module +
`conftest.py` + test module):
- `ci/testcase.py` — the `Spec` model + loaders + the planner **CLI** (`lint`/`matrix`/
  `select`). No pytest dependency, so the lightweight plan job imports it freely.
- `ci/conftest.py` — the hooks/fixtures: `pytest_configure` registers **markers derived
  from the data** (so adding a category/driver needs no edit, and `--strict-markers`
  catches `-m` typos), `pytest_generate_tests` parametrizes + applies one marker per
  value + the ambient-XLEN filter, and the `sim_build` fixture builds each
  `(driver,CONFIGS)` once (the P4 fix). Cases run **serially within a cell** — the
  parallelism is across GitHub matrix cells, each its own build tree — so successive
  `CONFIGS` never clobber a `sim/` build that is still in use (see §6).
- `ci/test_runner.py` — the single `test_case` that shells out to `blackbox.sh`/`make`
  and asserts a clean exit. Every failure (and every build warning escalated to an
  error) is a real, red failure — except a case carrying a `known_issue:` reason in
  the catalog, which `conftest.py` turns into a tracked `xfail`: it still builds and
  runs, but its failure is expected and does not fail CI (an unexpected pass surfaces
  as `XPASS`). Reserve it for triaged, documented breakage.

No `pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini`: markers register dynamically in `conftest.py`,
`test_runner.py` is auto-discovered by the `test_` prefix, and the run passes `ci` as the
path. `blackbox.sh` is untouched; `regression.sh` is reduced to the four host/multi-step
backends (§5).

Selection is idiomatic pytest:

```
VX_XLEN=32 pytest ci -m "cache and simx and smoke" --strict-markers
pytest ci --collect-only -q -m "simx"      # dry-run
```

### 3.3 Cross-driver checks (`check: model_parity`)

SimX is the timing model of the RTL, not just a functional oracle. A case with
`check: model_parity` validates that: it is **not** driver-expanded — the runner
executes the same app/args/configs on **simx and rtlsim** as two legs of one case
(pinned to the rtlsim driver for build/matrix placement, since it elaborates the
RTL) and compares the runtime's final `PERF: instrs=…, cycles=…` summary:

- **instrs must match exactly** — both drivers are deterministic ISA-level
  executions, so any delta is functional divergence, not a timing gap;
- **cycles must agree within `tolerance`** (default 5%, per-case override).

Every case also prints a `PARITY:` line with both counts and the measured gap, so
green runs still leave a trend trail in the logs. The general-pipeline matrix
(vecadd, sgemm) lives in `ci/testcases/model_parity.yaml`; each extension
(tensor*, raytracing, graphics TEX/RASTER/OM, dxa) carries its own
`model_parity-*` case in its category file, with only that extension enabled so a
regression is attributable. Workloads are sized so steady state dominates
(>=~300k cycles for the pipeline cases) — a tiny kernel is all boot/dispatch skew
and makes the gap ratio noisy. A `model_parity` marker selects them all:
`pytest ci -m model_parity`. Use `known_issue:` (not a loosened tolerance) for a
tracked gap under investigation.

The `model_parity` category (`ci/testcases/model_parity.yaml`) is a **dedicated
cell**: because every `check: model_parity` case also carries the `model_parity`
marker, the `model_parity` cell runs `-m "model_parity and rtlsim"` and thereby
sweeps *every* parity case catalog-wide — one centralized simx↔RTL gate across
`{xlen 32, xlen 64}`. It runs at **`full`** tier (rtlsim-heavy → PR + nightly).
So a parity case never double-runs: category cells exclude the check markers
(`… and not model_parity and not perf_gate`); the check cells own them.

### 3.4 Perf-regression checks (`check: perf_gate`)

Same gating shape as §3.3 (its own dedicated cell driven by the `perf_gate`
marker, `full` tier, rtlsim-pinned) but a different assertion: instead of
comparing SimX vs RTL, it compares **this commit's rtlsim cycles against a
checked-in golden baseline** within ±2% (`ci/perf_baseline.py`). Because rtlsim
cycle counts are deterministic and host-independent, there is no noise to handle —
the threshold only absorbs benign, intended micro-changes.

- **Baselines** live in the source tree at `ci/perf/baselines/<category>.json`
  (canonical sorted JSON, one file per category). Each entry stores the measured
  `cycles`/`instrs` per xlen, plus a `config_hash` (of app/args/configs/shape)
  and the workload's `instrs` as **staleness guards**: if the run config changes
  (`config_hash` mismatch) or the workload changes (`instrs` mismatch), the check
  errors "regenerate" instead of comparing stale numbers.
- **Direction**: cycles above baseline by >tolerance = **regression** (hard fail);
  cycles below by >tolerance = an unlocked **improvement** — also fails, asking
  you to update the baseline so the gain is ratcheted in and a later silent
  regression back toward the old number is still caught.
- **Updating** is script-generated + human-reviewed, never done by CI:
  `pytest ci -m perf_gate --update-baselines` (a `conftest.py` option that
  flips `_perf_gate` from assert- to record-mode and flushes on session
  finish). A human runs it only for an intended perf change, reviews the JSON
  diff (`cycles: 999027 → 918400` = an explicit, reviewable perf delta), and
  commits. **CI must never pass `--update-baselines`** — an auto-updated baseline
  would silently absorb every regression. Same discipline as a golden image.
- Benchmarks **reuse the steady-state model_parity workloads** (base pipeline in
  `ci/testcases/perf_gate.yaml`; extensions as `perf_gate-*` cases in
  their category files) — one run, its own gate.

---

## 4. Workflow

### 4.1 `ci.yml` — catalog-driven

`plan` reads the data (via `testcase.py matrix`, no build env) and emits the
`(category × driver × xlen)` cell list for this event; each cell runs
`pytest ci -m "<category> and <driver>"` in its build tree, emits JUnit, and the run is
gated by a single `complete` job.

```
plan:  event × driver-policy × tier × (touches[] ∩ diff)  ->  cells JSON
setup: warm toolchain + third_party caches once (setup-vortex prepare=true)
build: one build tree per xlen, needs setup (restores the warmed caches)
tests: matrix = cells  ->  pytest ci -m "<cat> and <driver>" per cell  ->  JUnit
complete: single green gate (needs plan+setup+build+tests)
```

`setup` exists so a cold cache prepares the toolchain (a prebuilt-tarball download)
and third_party **once**, not once per xlen: the two `build` jobs `needs: setup` and
only restore. On a cache hit it is a fast no-op.

Driver/tier policy by event:

| Trigger | Drivers | Tier |
|---------|---------|------|
| push | simx | smoke |
| pull_request | simx, rtlsim | smoke,full |
| schedule (nightly/weekly) | all | all |
| workflow_dispatch | (inputs) | (inputs) |

This is the whole point: a push runs `simx` (the cheap, high-signal driver) and defers
the ~168 `rtlsim` runs to PR-gate/nightly — `--drivers=simx` is now just `-m "simx"`.

### 4.2 `setup-vortex` composite action

The cache/deps boilerplate (`read-version-pins + cache toolchain + cache third-party +
install deps + pip`) is one local composite action, parameterized by `profile`
(lite/full), used by every job. A `prepare` input (true only in the `setup` job) makes
it additionally **populate** the caches on a miss — building the toolchain + third_party
once — so build/test jobs (`prepare: false`) only ever restore. Prep logic lives in the
action, not duplicated across jobs.

### 4.3 `apptainer-ci.yml` — share setup, not orchestration

The Apptainer flow validates the build/test works **inside the `vortex.sif` container** —
an *environmental* signal, not functional coverage the host run already provides.
It is deliberately **not** folded into `ci.yml` (different intent → the wrong
abstraction). It stays a separate, minimal workflow that:
- **reuses** the `setup-vortex` composite action (genuinely identical host-side work), and
- runs a representative `pytest ci -m "regression and simx"` slice inside the container, not the
  full matrix.

Recommended triggers: weekly **offset** from the host weekly (so a failure is attributable
to the container, not the code) plus `paths:` on the container-definition files.

---

## 5. Migration — done

The catalog is now the **single source of truth**; `ci/regression.sh.in` no longer
duplicates any cataloged test. Final shape:

- **25 categories native** in the catalog (`via: blackbox`/`make-run`/`script`), including
  the host categories `unittest`, `synthesis`, `vector` (self-contained `via: script` that
  call `make` directly — no `regression.sh`).
- **MX coverage is first-class:** `tensor_mx` (transcribed from the legacy `tensor_mx()`,
  incl. a `-DTCU_MX_TLS` tensor-level-scale variant) and `tensor_sp_mx` are catalog
  categories. `TCU_MX_TLS` is a **sw/test macro** passed per-case in `configs`, **not** a
  hardware `VX_CFG_` knob (it is not in `VX_config.toml`).
- **4 host/multi-step categories** (`dtm`, `sst`, `gem5`, `cupbop`) stay `via: script`
  delegating to `./ci/regression.sh --<cat>`. These are genuinely multi-step host flows
  (special builds: `USE_SST=1`/`USE_GEM5=1`, the gem5 ARM matrix, a cupbop download) that
  don't fit the common shape, so `regression.sh.in` is **kept on purpose** — slimmed from
  ~1400 lines to ~320, holding only those four functions. This is the documented
  steady state, not a pending deletion.
- **440 test cases / 31 categories**; `ci/testcase.py lint` + `pytest --collect-only` clean.
- Local runs go through `ci/regression.sh` against the **same** catalog CI runs, so
  they can never drift from it: `./ci/regression.sh --all` runs every category for the
  build tree's XLEN, and `./ci/regression.sh --test "<selector>"` runs a slice, where
  `<selector>` is a pytest marker expression — a category (`tensor`), a driver
  (`rtlsim`), or a combo (`"tensor and simx"`). Both wrap `pytest [-m …] ci`.

Real per-category sim execution runs on CI, not locally.

### 5.1 Graphics / Vulkan fixed-function coverage

The graphics stack is swept along the **fixed-function (FF) axis** — each of TEX /
RASTER / OM either present in hardware or emulated in SIMT software — because the
FF↔SIMT boundary is the recurring graphics bug surface:

- **Native FF units** (`graphics`): `gfx_tex` / `gfx_raster` / `gfx_om` each drive
  one FF unit; `gfx_draw3d` drives all three (TEX+RASTER+OM).
- **Early-Z** (`graphics`, `gfx_earlyz-*`): `gfx_draw3d` built with
  `-DVX_CFG_RASTER_EARLYZ` — the opt-in occlusion-cull knob (legal only with
  OM+RASTER; off by default → raster byte-identical). Bit-identical to the
  no-early-Z golden on box@128 / evilskull@32 (simx + rtlsim); evilskull@128
  carries a tracked 2-px in-flight-write residual (`known_issue`).
- **FF/SW mix + full software emulation** (`vulkan`, `ff-*`): the vortexpipe 3D
  pipeline (`draw3d`) with per-unit drop knobs — `NO_TEX` / `NO_RASTER` / `NO_OM`
  (`tests/vulkan/common.mk`) — sweeps every FF/SW combination
  (`ff-raster-tex-om` … `ff-om-only`, and `ff-all-sw` = whole pipeline in SIMT
  software). vortexpipe routes each dropped unit to the `gfx_*_sw` ABI, validated
  against the same golden as the all-hardware path. Combos that need SW-TEX or
  SW-RASTER routing are `known_issue` until vortexpipe wires those stages (the SW
  ABI already exists).
- **Ray tracing + hybrid** (`vulkan`): `rt-raytrace` / `rt-rtquery` (VK_KHR_ray_query
  benchmarks on the PRISM RTU), `gfx-rt-rtquery-id` (rasterized fragment shader +
  inline ray query — gfx + RT in one frame), and `gfx-multidraw` (multi-drawcall
  rasterization). The blanket `vulkan` `isa-*` cases still run the whole suite per
  driver; these track the individual scenarios and add the FF/SW-mix builds the
  suite does not produce.

New cases in these yaml files are auto-included in the plan (§4.1) — no workflow
edit needed. `known_issue` cases still build and run (surfacing an `XPASS` when the
underlying support lands), so aspirational coverage is tracked, not silently absent.

---

## 6. Risks & mitigations

- **Build-dedup vs. parallelism (resolved).** Successive `CONFIGS` build into the same
  `sim/` output, so building different keys concurrently in one tree clobbers them — this
  was confirmed on the first CI run (an in-tree `pytest -n auto` raced multiple Verilator
  builds and most cells errored). Resolution: **cases run serially within a cell**, and
  parallelism is taken **across GitHub matrix cells** (each cell is its own runner +
  build tree). A future intra-cell speedup would need per-worker isolated trees
  (`git worktree`); not worth it now.
- **Data drifts from reality.** `testcase.py lint` runs in CI; each migrated category is
  parity-diffed against its legacy function once before the bash is deleted.
- **Script categories.** `via: script` lets the special categories delegate to legacy
  without forcing them into the common shape; their `needs` deps must be provisioned by
  the workflow (a missing dep is a real failure — nothing is skipped).
- **pytest dependency.** Industry standard; Python is already on the CI path; pinned like
  any dev tool. The harness only orchestrates and shells out.
- **Catalog format: YAML** — list-of-records ergonomics, PyYAML/Actions-native; TOML is
  awkward for record arrays, JSON loses comments.

"""pytest hooks + fixtures for the Vortex test cases.

Registers markers dynamically from the data, turns each test case
(ci/testcase.py) into a parametrized pytest item, and builds each sim once per
build-key. The test itself is ci/test_runner.py. No pytest config file is
needed — markers and collection are handled here. Run from a build tree:

  VX_XLEN=32 pytest ci -m "amo and simx" --strict-markers --dist=loadgroup -n auto

See docs/designs/continuous_integration.md.
"""

import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import testcase as tc  # noqa: E402


def ambient_xlen():
    """The XLEN of the build tree pytest runs in (build32/ or build64/)."""
    return int(os.environ.get("VX_XLEN", "32"))


def pytest_addoption(parser):
    # perf_gate record-mode: measure and rewrite the golden cycle
    # baselines instead of asserting against them. Human-run + reviewed; CI
    # never passes this flag. See ci/perf_baseline.py.
    parser.addoption("--update-baselines", action="store_true", default=False,
                     help="perf_gate: record measured cycles into "
                          "ci/perf/baselines/ instead of comparing")


def pytest_sessionfinish(session):
    if session.config.getoption("--update-baselines"):
        import perf_baseline
        perf_baseline.flush()


def pytest_configure(config):
    # Register every marker the test cases use, derived from the data — so adding
    # a category/driver needs no edit here. With --strict-markers this also makes
    # a typo'd `-m` expression an error instead of a silent empty selection.
    for marker in sorted({m for c in tc.load_all() for m in c.markers()}):
        config.addinivalue_line("markers", "{}: test-case selector".format(marker))


def pytest_generate_tests(metafunc):
    if "case" not in metafunc.fixturenames:
        return
    xlen = ambient_xlen()
    params = []
    for case in tc.load_all():
        if not case.applies_to_xlen(xlen):
            continue
        marks = [getattr(pytest.mark, name) for name in case.markers()]
        if case.known_issue:
            # Tracked expected-failure: the case still builds and runs (so its
            # logs and an unexpected pass are visible as XPASS), but its failure
            # does not fail CI. strict=False tolerates an XPASS rather than
            # converting it to a hard failure.
            marks.append(pytest.mark.xfail(reason="known issue: " + case.known_issue,
                                           strict=False))
        params.append(pytest.param(case, marks=marks, id=case.id))
    metafunc.parametrize("case", params)


# Sim builds are deduped per (driver, configs) build-key. Cases run serially
# within a cell (parallelism is across GitHub matrix cells, each its own build
# tree), so this cache builds each sim once and successive CONFIGS never clobber
# a build that is still in use.
_BUILT = set()


@pytest.fixture
def sim_build(case):
    if not case.needs_sim:        # driverless via:script cases self-build
        return None
    # blackbox cases build their own sim at run time with the FULL flag set
    # (configs + the shape-derived -DVX_CFG_NUM_* defines that blackbox.sh
    # appends). A fixture pre-build here uses configs only, so it would compile
    # a shape-stripped config the test never runs — e.g. NUM_TEX_CORES without
    # the matching core count, which elaborates an unreachable arbiter geometry
    # and trips spurious Verilator width lints — and blackbox would rebuild it
    # anyway. Let the run own the build; the sim Makefile's flag stamp clears a
    # stale obj_dir on any flag change, so cross-config builds stay clean.
    if case.via == "blackbox":
        return None
    key = case.build_key()
    if key not in _BUILT:
        # Clean first: a new CONFIGS must not reuse the previous config's obj_dir
        # (stale Verilator state -> spurious lint errors). Legacy does the same:
        # `make -C sim/<d> clean && CONFIGS=… make -C sim/<d>`.
        tc.execute(["make", "-C", case.sim_dir, "clean"])
        argv, env = case.build_command(ambient_xlen())
        rc = tc.execute(argv, env)
        if rc != 0:
            pytest.fail("sim build failed (exit {}): {}".format(rc, " ".join(argv)))
        _BUILT.add(key)
    return key

12	XPASS). Use it only for triaged, documented breakage.
13	
14	A `check: model_parity` case runs the same app/args/configs on simx and rtlsim
15	and compares the runtime's final `PERF: instrs=…, cycles=…` summary: retired
16	instructions must match exactly (both are deterministic ISA-level executions,
17	so any delta is functional divergence) and cycles must agree within the case's
18	`tolerance` (SimX is the timing model of the RTL, not just a functional oracle).
19	"""

"""The Vortex test case.

Every catalog entry becomes one `test_case` item (parametrization, markers and
the sim_build fixture live in ci/conftest.py). The body shells out to the
existing executor (blackbox.sh / make) and asserts a clean exit, so those stay
the execution primitives. See docs/designs/continuous_integration.md.

Every failure (and every warning the build escalates to an error) is a real, red
failure — the one exception is a case carrying a `known_issue:` reason in the
catalog, which conftest turns into a tracked xfail: it still builds and runs, but
its failure is expected and does not fail CI (and an unexpected pass shows as
XPASS). Use it only for triaged, documented breakage.

A `check: model_parity` case runs the same app/args/configs on simx and rtlsim
and compares the runtime's final `PERF: instrs=…, cycles=…` summary: retired
instructions must match exactly (both are deterministic ISA-level executions,
so any delta is functional divergence) and cycles must agree within the case's
`tolerance` (SimX is the timing model of the RTL, not just a functional oracle).
"""

import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import testcase as tc  # noqa: E402
import perf_baseline as pb  # noqa: E402

# The device-level summary vx_device_dump_perf always prints (per-core lines
# have a `coreN:` prefix and don't match). cycles is max across cores.
_PERF_RE = re.compile(r"^PERF: instrs=(\d+), cycles=(\d+), IPC=", re.M)


def _run_one(case, xlen, driver):
    """One parity leg: run under `driver`, return (instrs, cycles)."""
    argv, env = case.run_command(xlen, driver=driver)
    rc, out = tc.execute_capture(argv, env)
    assert rc == 0, "{} [{}] failed (exit {}): {}".format(
        case.id, driver, rc, " ".join(argv))
    perf = _PERF_RE.findall(out)
    assert perf, "{} [{}]: no 'PERF: instrs=…, cycles=…' summary in output " \
                 "(app must call vx_device_dump_perf)".format(case.id, driver)
    instrs, cycles = perf[-1]
    return int(instrs), int(cycles)


def _model_parity(case, xlen):
    simx_instrs, simx_cycles = _run_one(case, xlen, "simx")
    rtl_instrs, rtl_cycles = _run_one(case, xlen, "rtlsim")
    gap = abs(rtl_cycles - simx_cycles) / float(rtl_cycles)
    print("PARITY: {}: instrs simx={} rtlsim={}, cycles simx={} rtlsim={}, "
          "gap={:.2%} (tolerance {:.0%})".format(
              case.id, simx_instrs, rtl_instrs, simx_cycles, rtl_cycles,
              gap, case.tolerance))
    assert simx_instrs == rtl_instrs, \
        "{}: retired-instruction mismatch (simx={}, rtlsim={}) — functional " \
        "divergence, not a timing gap".format(case.id, simx_instrs, rtl_instrs)
    assert gap <= case.tolerance, \
        "{}: cycle gap {:.2%} exceeds tolerance {:.0%} (simx={}, rtlsim={})".format(
            case.id, gap, case.tolerance, simx_cycles, rtl_cycles)


def _perf_gate(case, xlen, update):
    """Run the benchmark on rtlsim; record or compare its cycles vs baseline."""
    instrs, cycles = _run_one(case, xlen, "rtlsim")
    if update:
        pb.record(case, xlen, cycles, instrs)
        print("PERF-BASELINE: {} xlen={} record cycles={} instrs={}".format(
            case.id, xlen, cycles, instrs))
        return
    cat = pb.load(case.category)
    base = cat.get(case.id)
    assert base, "{}: no perf baseline — run pytest --update-baselines".format(case.id)
    assert base.get("config_hash") == pb.config_hash(case), \
        "{}: baseline stale (run config changed) — regenerate with " \
        "--update-baselines".format(case.id)
    ref = base.get(str(xlen))
    assert ref, "{}: no perf baseline at xlen {} — regenerate".format(case.id, xlen)
    assert instrs == ref["instrs"], \
        "{}: workload changed (instrs {} != baseline {}) — regenerate " \
        "baseline".format(case.id, instrs, ref["instrs"])
    ratio = cycles / float(ref["cycles"])
    print("PERF: {}: cycles={} baseline={} ratio={:.3f} (tolerance +/-{:.0%})".format(
        case.id, cycles, ref["cycles"], ratio, pb.TOLERANCE))
    assert ratio <= 1 + pb.TOLERANCE, \
        "{}: perf REGRESSION — cycles {} exceed baseline {} by {:.1%} " \
        "(> {:.0%})".format(case.id, cycles, ref["cycles"], ratio - 1, pb.TOLERANCE)
    assert ratio >= 1 - pb.TOLERANCE, \
        "{}: perf IMPROVEMENT of {:.1%} beyond ratchet — rerun " \
        "--update-baselines to lock the gain in (baseline={}, now={})".format(
            case.id, 1 - ratio, ref["cycles"], cycles)


def test_case(case, sim_build, request):
    xlen = int(os.environ.get("VX_XLEN", "32"))
    if case.check == "model_parity":
        _model_parity(case, xlen)
        return
    if case.check == "perf_gate":
        _perf_gate(case, xlen, request.config.getoption("--update-baselines"))
        return
    argv, env = case.run_command(xlen)
    rc = tc.execute(argv, env)
    assert rc == 0, "{} failed (exit {}): {}".format(case.id, rc, " ".join(argv))

52	    """One concrete test case: a single (category, driver, configs, shape) point."""
53	
54	    def __init__(self, category, entry, driver, defaults):
55	        self.category = category
56	        self.driver = driver
57	        self.via = entry.get("via", "blackbox")
58	        self.app = entry.get("app", "")
59	        self.args = entry.get("args", "")
60	        # Verbatim extra blackbox flags the structured fields don't model
61	        # (e.g. --debug=3 --perf=6 --scope --nohup --log=...).
62	        self.flags = entry.get("flags", "")
63	        self.shape = dict(entry.get("shape", {}))
64	        self.tier = entry.get("tier", defaults.get("tier", "smoke"))
65	        self.needs = list(entry.get("needs", defaults.get("needs", [])))
66	        self.touches = list(entry.get("touches", defaults.get("touches", [])))
67	        self.xlens = [int(x) for x in entry.get("xlen", defaults.get("xlen", [32, 64]))]
68	        self.configs = _merge_configs(defaults.get("configs", ""), entry)

70	        # expected-failure (pytest xfail). The case still runs and reports, but
71	        # its failure does not fail CI. Falls back to the file-level default so a
72	        # wholly-broken category can mark every case in one place.
73	        self.known_issue = entry.get("known_issue", defaults.get("known_issue", ""))

75	        # both simx and rtlsim and asserts the reported cycle counts agree within

83	        # default (which still governs that file's functional cases), so 64-bit
84	        # coverage can't creep back in per-file.
85	        if self.check in ("model_parity", "perf_gate"):

91	        self.dir = entry.get("dir", "")
92	        self.target = entry.get("target", "")
93	        self.run = entry.get("run", "")
94	        self.vars = dict(entry.get("vars", {}))
95	        # Stable, unique id: <category>:<authored-id>:<marker-driver>
96	        self.id = "{}:{}:{}".format(category, entry["id"], self.marker_driver)
97	
98	    @property
99	    def marker_driver(self):
100	        return driver_marker(self.driver) if self.driver else None
101	
102	    @property
103	    def needs_sim(self):
104	        """Whether a sim build is required (driverless via:script cases self-build)."""
105	        return self.via != "script" and self.driver is not None
106	
107	    @property
108	    def sim_dir(self):
109	        return "sim/" + _DRIVER_TO_SIMDIR[self.driver]
110	
111	    def build_key(self):
112	        """What determines a *sim build*. `via` is deliberately excluded so a
113	        make-run case and a blackbox case with the same (driver, configs) share
114	        one sim build. xlen is implicit in the ambient tree.
115	        """
116	        return (self.driver, self.configs)
117	
118	    def markers(self):
119	        """pytest marker names for `-m` selection (one per value)."""
120	        m = [self.category, self.tier]
121	        if self.marker_driver:
122	            m.append(self.marker_driver)
123	        if self.check:
124	            m.append(self.check)
125	        m += ["needs_{}".format(n) for n in self.needs]
126	        return m
127	
128	    def applies_to_xlen(self, xlen):
129	        return int(xlen) in self.xlens
130	
131	    def build_command(self, xlen):
132	        """argv + env to build this case's sim once (shared across build_key)."""
133	        env = {"CONFIGS": _subst(self.configs, xlen)} if self.configs else {}
134	        return ["make", "-C", self.sim_dir], env
135	
136	    def run_command(self, xlen, driver=None):
137	        """argv + env to execute this case at the given ambient xlen. `driver`
138	        overrides the case's own driver (the cycle-parity runner uses it to
139	        drive both legs of one case)."""
140	        env = {"CONFIGS": _subst(self.configs, xlen)} if self.configs else {}
141	        if self.via == "blackbox":
142	            argv = ["./ci/blackbox.sh", "--driver=" + (driver or self.driver),
143	                    "--app=" + self.app]
144	            argv += _shape_flags(self.shape)
145	            if self.args:
146	                argv.append("--args=" + self.args)
147	            if self.flags:
148	                argv += self.flags.split()
149	            return argv, env
150	        if self.via == "make-run":
151	            target = self.target.format(driver=self.driver, xlen=xlen)
152	            argv = ["make", "-C", self.dir, target]
153	            argv += ["{}={}".format(k, v) for k, v in self.vars.items()]
154	            return argv, env
155	        if self.via == "script":
156	            # run through a shell so multi-step `cmd1 && cmd2` scripts work.
157	            return ["bash", "-c", _subst(self.run, xlen)], env
158	        raise ValueError("unknown via: {!r}".format(self.via))
159	
160	
161	def _subst(text, xlen):
162	    """Resolve the ambient-xlen placeholders in a config/run string:
163	    {xlen} -> 32/64, {xsize} -> XLEN/8 (the legacy $XLEN / $XSIZE)."""
164	    return text.replace("{xlen}", str(xlen)).replace("{xsize}", str(int(xlen) // 8))
165	
166	
167	def _merge_configs(default, entry):
168	    """`configs` overrides the default; `configs+` appends to it."""
169	    if "configs" in entry:
170	        return entry["configs"]
171	    if "configs+" in entry:
172	        return (default + " " + entry["configs+"]).strip()
173	    return default
174	
175	
176	def _shape_flags(shape):
177	    flags = []
178	    for knob in ("clusters", "cores", "warps", "threads"):
179	        if shape.get(knob):
180	            flags.append("--{}={}".format(knob, shape[knob]))
181	    for boolean in ("l2cache", "l3cache", "scope"):
182	        if shape.get(boolean):
183	            flags.append("--" + boolean)
184	    return flags
185	
186	
187	def load_category(path):
188	    """Expand one testcases YAML file into concrete cases."""
189	    with open(path) as fh:
190	        doc = yaml.safe_load(fh)
191	    category = doc["category"]
192	    defaults = doc.get("defaults", {})
193	    cases = []
194	    for entry in doc.get("tests", []):
195	        # via:script cases may be driverless (host/synthesis); everything else
196	        # has a driver or a drivers list. A check: case is never driver-expanded
197	        # — it is one case pinned to rtlsim that runs both drivers itself.
198	        if entry.get("check"):
199	            drivers = ["rtlsim"]
200	        else:
201	            drivers = entry.get("drivers") or ([entry["driver"]] if "driver" in entry else [None])
202	        for driver in drivers:
203	            cases.append(Spec(category, entry, driver, defaults))
204	    return cases
205	
206	
207	def load_all(testcases_dir=TESTCASES_DIR):
208	    """Load every ci/testcases/*.yaml into a flat list of concrete cases."""
209	    cases = []
210	    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(testcases_dir, "*.yaml"))):
211	        cases.extend(load_category(path))
212	    return cases
213	
214	
215	def execute(argv, env_extra=None, cwd=None):
216	    """Run argv with CONFIGS et al. merged into the environment; return exit code."""
217	    env = dict(os.environ)
218	    if env_extra:
219	        env.update(env_extra)
220	    return subprocess.run(argv, env=env, cwd=cwd).returncode
221	
222	
223	def execute_capture(argv, env_extra=None, cwd=None):
224	    """Like execute(), but also return the combined stdout/stderr text. Output
225	    is still echoed line-by-line so CI logs keep the full run."""
226	    env = dict(os.environ)
227	    if env_extra:
228	        env.update(env_extra)
229	    proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, env=env, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
230	                            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, errors="replace")
231	    lines = []
232	    for line in proc.stdout:
233	        sys.stdout.write(line)
234	        lines.append(line)
235	    proc.stdout.close()
236	    return proc.wait(), "".join(lines)

238	
239	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
240	# Planner CLI — lint / matrix / select. Reads the same data the harness runs,
241	# but needs no pytest or build env, so the ci.yml plan job can call it.
242	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
243	
244	# A changed file under one of these prefixes FORCES the listed sim driver(s)
245	# into the run regardless of the event tier — the RTL is shared by every sim
246	# backend and simx (a separate C++ model) cannot exercise it, so an RTL change
247	# with simx-only coverage is effectively untested. rtlsim is the cheapest driver
248	# that elaborates the RTL; AFU/host-surface paths additionally need xrt/opae.
249	_DRIVER_PATHS = [
250	    ("hw/rtl/afu/", ("rtlsim", "xrt", "opae")),
251	    ("hw/rtl/", ("rtlsim",)),
252	    ("hw/dpi/", ("rtlsim",)),
253	    ("sim/rtlsim/", ("rtlsim",)),
254	    ("sim/xrtsim/", ("xrt",)),
255	    ("sim/opaesim/", ("opae",)),
256	    ("third_party/cvfpu/", ("rtlsim",)),
257	    ("third_party/hardfloat/", ("rtlsim",)),
258	    # Config inputs regenerate the RTL parameters, so exercise the RTL too.
259	    ("VX_config.toml", ("rtlsim",)),
260	    ("VX_types.toml", ("rtlsim",)),
261	    ("vortex_opae.toml", ("opae",)),
262	]
263	
264	
265	def drivers_for_changes(changed):
266	    """Set of execution-driver names a diff forces in (path->driver escalation)."""
267	    out = set()
268	    for f in changed:
269	        for prefix, drvs in _DRIVER_PATHS:
270	            if f.startswith(prefix):
271	                out.update(drvs)
272	    return out
273	
274	
275	def _changed_files(ref):
276	    """Files changed vs `ref`, or None if the diff is indeterminate (bad/zero
277	    base, missing history) — callers treat None as 'fall back to full coverage'."""
278	    out = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--name-only", ref + "...HEAD"],
279	                         capture_output=True, text=True)
280	    if out.returncode != 0:  # fall back to a two-dot diff if no merge base
281	        out = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--name-only", ref],
282	                             capture_output=True, text=True)
283	    if out.returncode != 0:
284	        return None
285	    return [line for line in out.stdout.splitlines() if line]
286	
287	
288	def _touched(case, changed):
289	    return any(f.startswith(prefix) for prefix in case.touches for f in changed)
290	
291	
292	def _filter(cases, args):
293	    drivers = set(args.drivers.split(",")) if getattr(args, "drivers", None) else None
294	    tiers = set(args.tier.split(",")) if getattr(args, "tier", None) else None
295	    changed = _changed_files(args.changed_from) if getattr(args, "changed_from", None) else None
296	    out = []
297	    for c in cases:
298	        if drivers and c.marker_driver not in drivers:
299	            continue
300	        if tiers and c.tier not in tiers:
301	            continue
302	        # Path-scaling: only a case that DECLARES touches is subject to the diff
303	        # filter. A case with no touches has no path opinion and always runs, so
304	        # enabling --changed-from never silently drops an un-annotated category.
305	        if changed is not None and c.touches and not _touched(c, changed):
306	            continue
307	        out.append(c)
308	    return out
309	
310	
311	def cmd_matrix(args):
312	    # One GitHub matrix cell per (category, driver, xlen): the build tree is
313	    # per-xlen, so xlen is flattened out (not a per-cell list).
314	    xfilter = {int(x) for x in args.xlen.split(",")} if getattr(args, "xlen", None) else None
315	    cells = {}
316	    for c in _filter(load_all(), args):
317	        drv = c.marker_driver or "host"
318	        for xlen in c.xlens:
319	            if xfilter and xlen not in xfilter:
320	                continue
321	            key = (c.category, drv, xlen)
322	            cell = cells.setdefault(key, {
323	                "category": c.category, "driver": drv, "xlen": xlen, "needs": set(),
324	            })
325	            cell["needs"].update(c.needs)
326	    out = []
327	    for cell in cells.values():
328	        cell["needs"] = sorted(cell["needs"])
329	        out.append(cell)
330	    out.sort(key=lambda c: (c["category"], c["driver"], c["xlen"]))
331	    print(json.dumps(out))
332	    return 0
333	
334	
335	def cmd_select(args):
336	    print(" ".join(sorted({c.category for c in _filter(load_all(), args)})))
337	    return 0
338	
339	
340	def cmd_drivers(args):
341	    """Execution drivers a diff forces in (path->driver escalation). Prints 'ALL'
342	    when the diff is indeterminate (zero/empty/missing base) so the caller falls
343	    back to full driver coverage rather than under-testing."""
344	    ref = getattr(args, "changed_from", None)
345	    if not ref or set(ref) <= set("0"):
346	        print("ALL")
347	        return 0
348	    changed = _changed_files(ref)
349	    if changed is None:
350	        print("ALL")
351	        return 0
352	    print(",".join(sorted(drivers_for_changes(changed))))
353	    return 0
354	
355	
356	def cmd_lint(args):
357	    cases = load_all()
358	    errors, seen = [], {}
359	    for c in cases:
360	        if c.id in seen:
361	            errors.append("duplicate id: {}".format(c.id))
362	        seen[c.id] = c
363	        if c.via not in VALID_VIA:
364	            errors.append("{}: invalid via {!r}".format(c.id, c.via))
365	        if c.driver is not None and c.driver not in VALID_DRIVERS:
366	            errors.append("{}: invalid driver {!r}".format(c.id, c.driver))
367	        if c.via == "blackbox" and not c.app:
368	            errors.append("{}: blackbox case missing 'app'".format(c.id))
369	        if c.via == "make-run" and not (c.dir and c.target):
370	            errors.append("{}: make-run case needs 'dir' and 'target'".format(c.id))
371	        if c.via == "script" and not c.run:
372	            errors.append("{}: script case missing 'run'".format(c.id))
373	        if any(int(x) not in (32, 64) for x in c.xlens):
374	            errors.append("{}: xlen must be 32 and/or 64".format(c.id))
375	        if c.check:
376	            if c.check not in VALID_CHECK:
377	                errors.append("{}: invalid check {!r}".format(c.id, c.check))
378	            if c.via != "blackbox":
379	                errors.append("{}: check cases must be via blackbox".format(c.id))
380	            if c.authored_drivers:
381	                errors.append("{}: check cases must not set driver/drivers "
382	                              "(the runner drives simx and rtlsim)".format(c.id))
383	            if not (0.0 < c.tolerance < 1.0):
384	                errors.append("{}: tolerance must be in (0, 1)".format(c.id))
385	    if errors:
386	        for e in errors:
387	            sys.stderr.write("LINT ERROR: " + e + "\n")
388	        return 1
389	    print("OK: {} test cases across {} categories".format(
390	        len(cases), len({c.category for c in cases})))
391	    return 0
392	
393	
394	def main(argv=None):
395	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Vortex test-case planner")
396	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
397	
398	    m = sub.add_parser("matrix", help="emit JSON (category x driver x xlen) cells")
399	    m.add_argument("--drivers")
400	    m.add_argument("--tier")
401	    m.add_argument("--xlen")
402	    m.add_argument("--changed-from", dest="changed_from")
403	    m.set_defaults(func=cmd_matrix)
404	
405	    s = sub.add_parser("select", help="categories whose touches[] hit a diff")
406	    s.add_argument("--drivers")
407	    s.add_argument("--tier")
408	    s.add_argument("--changed-from", dest="changed_from")
409	    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_select)
410	
411	    d = sub.add_parser("drivers", help="drivers a diff forces in (path->driver)")
412	    d.add_argument("--changed-from", dest="changed_from")
413	    d.set_defaults(func=cmd_drivers)
414	
415	    sub.add_parser("lint", help="validate the test cases").set_defaults(func=cmd_lint)
416	
417	    args = p.parse_args(argv)
418	    return args.func(args)
419	
420	
421	if __name__ == "__main__":
422	    sys.exit(main())
